content.text: Team: M. Bilal Tahir (24i-3166), Taimoor Shaukat (24i-3015) — Section SE-B.
Project under test: agentMom (broadcast/multicast/secured communication SRS enhancement). Repo: https://github.com/IfBilal/agent-mom-sqe, frozen baseline commit e79b197.

Part 3.B executed all 15 designed test cases against the frozen baseline (evidence/test-execution/). Two produced a genuine non-PASSED status by design: TC-08 (FAILED) and TC-11 (BLOCKED). Per the assignment brief, every FAILED/BLOCKED case plus every SonarQube finding with a plausible functional angle was investigated before deciding whether it represents a defect.

4 candidates investigated. 0 met all 4 defect criteria (executed; actual != expected; reproduced >= 2x; not explained by an already-declared assumption/limitation). All 4 are logged below as Done / Low priority, each with full investigation notes and a link back to the source evidence — this documents that the investigation happened and why each was excluded, rather than leaving an empty board with no audit trail.
KAN-5 — TC-08 / setMulticastTTL(0) confinement — environment limitation (no router on single-host test bed)
KAN-6 — TC-11 / LAN-wide broadcast reach — precondition unmet (no second host)
KAN-7 — SonarQube F1 / crypto sort — investigated, functionally correct
KAN-8 — SonarQube F4 / JSX spacing — investigated, no rendering fault

content.text: agentmom-se3002, frozen baseline commit e79b197 (evidence/BASELINE_TAG_HASH.txt), triage executed 2026-09-07
Demo topology running (agent-A..D); single physical machine, no router in the network path.
Send a group-alpha multicast with a positive envelope TTL (isolating the level-1 OS TTL as the only possible confinement mechanism).
Record which co-located agents receive it.
Per SRS section 1.3 (TTL defined as router-hop count), setMulticastTTL(0) confines the datagram to the originating host — no other agent should receive it.
agent-C, agent-B, and agent-D all received it. Console evidence: "[TC-08] co-located receivers observed for a group-alpha multicast: agent-C, agent-B, agent-D".
Always — deterministic every run (3/3 in the triage session; consistent across CI history).
N/A — not a defect (see investigation below). If it were a defect it would be Low severity, Low priority.

SRS section 1.3 defines TTL as a router-hop counter. On same-host delivery no router is traversed, so the mechanism has nothing to act on. Code inspection confirms socket.setMulticastTTL() is called correctly (packages/agent/src/transports/multicast-transport.ts). The implementation matches the SRS; the test bed cannot exercise router-hop scope. Declared in advance in DEVIATIONS.md D-5 and evidence/PHASE-10-VERIFICATION.md.
NOT A DEFECT — environment limitation (single-host test bed has no router).

Full evidence: https://github.com/IfBilal/agent-mom-sqe/blob/main/evidence/test-execution/npm-test-output-verbose.txt (search TC-08) and https://github.com/IfBilal/agent-mom-sqe/blob/main/DEVIATIONS.md#d-5. Test source: packages/control-plane/tests/integration/fr3-ttl.test.ts.

content.text: agentmom-se3002, frozen baseline commit e79b197 (evidence/BASELINE_TAG_HASH.txt), triage executed 2026-09-07
Required: a multi-host local network so 'all possible hosts' can be enumerated and receipt confirmed on each. Available: one physical machine only (dns-HP-EliteBook-640-14-inch-G10-Notebook-PC).
Attempt to confirm broadcast receipt on a second host on the same local network.
Per SRS 3.2.3.3, a broadcast is sent to all possible hosts under the same local network.

The required precondition (>=2 hosts on the same LAN) does not exist on this test bed — confirmed by verify-preconditions.sh (one host, 5 network interfaces, zero reachable peers). This is not a claim that LAN-wide delivery failed; it was never executed at LAN scope. TC-10 already confirms host-local delivery works (all 4 agents receive).
N/A — BLOCKED status means the case could not execute, not that it executed and failed.
Declared in advance in ASSUMPTIONS.md A4.1/A4.2. The precondition (multi-host LAN) simply does not exist on this development/test machine.
NOT A DEFECT — precondition unmet (no second host available to test against).

Full evidence: https://github.com/IfBilal/agent-mom-sqe/blob/main/evidence/test-execution/TC-11-single-host-network-interfaces.txt and https://github.com/IfBilal/agent-mom-sqe/blob/main/ASSUMPTIONS.md (A4.1/A4.2). TC-10 (host-local, PASSED) confirms the send/receive logic itself works.

content.text: agentmom-se3002, frozen baseline commit e79b197 (evidence/BASELINE_TAG_HASH.txt), triage executed 2026-09-07 — packages/core/src/crypto/symmetric.ts:59
Inspect derivePairwiseKey(): sorts [agentA, agentB] with the default comparator, joins, and hashes.
Rule S2871 flags default Array.sort() as producing an unreliable/locale-dependent order.

derivePairwiseKey produces an identical, correctly order-independent key on every run. JavaScript's default comparator sorts ASCII strings by UTF-16 code-unit order, which is deterministic and NOT locale-dependent for this input. Applying Sonar's own suggested fix (localeCompare) would make the ordering locale-dependent — the opposite of what a hash canonicalization step needs, and would introduce the exact class of bug the rule exists to prevent.
N/A — no failure to reproduce; the derivation is confirmed correct on every run.
N/A — not a defect. Flagged by SonarQube as Critical/Reliability, but investigation shows no functional fault.
NOT A DEFECT — true-positive static pattern, confirmed functionally correct for this specific usage on manual investigation.
SonarQube Part 3.A Finding F1; core/tests/unit/crypto.test.ts COND-36

Full evidence: https://github.com/IfBilal/agent-mom-sqe/blob/main/packages/core/tests/unit/crypto.test.ts (COND-36) and https://github.com/IfBilal/agent-mom-sqe/blob/main/packages/core/src/crypto/symmetric.ts#L59.
